hints: Consider particle A in equilibrium under three coplanar forces: downward weight $0.2g = 2\text{ N}$, horizontal tension $T_{AB}$ to the right, and tension $T_{AP}$ along string AP at $45^\circ$ to the ceiling.
Resolve vertically at particle A to find $T_{AP} \sin 45^\circ = 2\text{ N}$.
Resolve horizontally at particle A to relate $T_{AB}$ to $T_{AP} \cos 45^\circ$, and deduce $T_{AB} = 2\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces vertically at particle A in equilibrium, where weight is $0.2g = 2\text{ N}$ and string AP makes $45^\circ$ with the horizontal ceiling:
$$T_{AP} \sin 45^\circ - 0.2g = 0 \implies T_{AP} \sin 45^\circ = 2\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces horizontally at particle A to find the tension $T_{AB}$:
$$T_{AB} = T_{AP} \cos 45^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Consider the equilibrium of particle A of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$. The forces acting on A are:
1. Downward weight: $W_A = m_A g = 0.2 \times 10 = 2\text{ N}$.
2. Tension in string AP, denoted $T_{AP}$, acting upward and to the left at an angle of $45^\circ$ to the horizontal ceiling.
3. Tension in the horizontal string AB, denoted $T_{AB}$, pulling horizontally to the right.

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation for particle A:
$$T_{AP} \sin 45^\circ - W_A = 0$$
$$T_{AP} \sin 45^\circ = 2$$
$$T_{AP} = \frac{2}{\sin 45^\circ} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}/2} = 2\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$$

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation for particle A:
$$T_{AB} - T_{AP} \cos 45^\circ = 0$$
$$T_{AB} = T_{AP} \cos 45^\circ$$

hints: Consider particle B in equilibrium under downward weight $0.1g = 1\text{ N}$, tension $T_{AB} = 2\text{ N}$ pulling horizontally to the left, and tension $T_{BQ}$ at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal.
Form the horizontal and vertical equilibrium equations: $T_{BQ} \cos \theta = 2$ and $T_{BQ} \sin \theta = 1$.
Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to find $\tan \theta = 0.5$, then solve for $\theta$ and evaluate $T_{BQ} = \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve horizontally and vertically for particle B in equilibrium, with weight $0.1g = 1\text{ N}$ and $T_{AB} = 2\text{ N}$:
$$T_{BQ} \cos \theta = T_{AB} = 2$$
$$T_{BQ} \sin \theta = 0.1g = 1$$

Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to obtain $\tan \theta$:
$$\tan \theta = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5 \implies \theta = \arctan(0.5) \approx 26.6^\circ$$

Square and add both equations to find $T_{BQ}$:
$$T_{BQ}^2 = 2^2 + 1^2 = 4 + 1 = 5 \implies T_{BQ} = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Consider the equilibrium of particle B of mass $0.1\text{ kg}$. The forces acting on B are:
1. Downward weight: $W_B = m_B g = 0.1 \times 10 = 1\text{ N}$.
2. Horizontal tension from string AB pulling to the left: $T_{AB} = 2\text{ N}$.
3. Tension in string BQ, denoted $T_{BQ}$, pulling upward and to the right at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal ceiling.

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation:
$$\sum F_x = 0 \implies T_{BQ} \cos \theta - T_{AB} = 0$$
$$T_{BQ} \cos \theta = 2 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$\sum F_y = 0 \implies T_{BQ} \sin \theta - W_B = 0$$
$$T_{BQ} \sin \theta = 1 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 2 by Equation 1 to eliminate $T_{BQ}$:
$$\frac{T_{BQ} \sin \theta}{T_{BQ} \cos \theta} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\tan \theta = 0.5$$
$$\theta = \arctan(0.5) \approx 26.565^\circ \approx 26.6^\circ$$

To find $T_{BQ}$, square and add both equations:
$$(T_{BQ} \cos \theta)^2 + (T_{BQ} \sin \theta)^2 = 2^2 + 1^2$$
$$T_{BQ}^2 (\cos^2 \theta + \sin^2 \theta) = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$T_{BQ} = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.23607\text{ N} \approx 2.24\text{ N}$$
